## Cross-Cutting Findings from 11 Experiments

**1. Plausible order-flow narratives are not surviving out-of-sample, regardless of directional thesis.**
Underlying assumption failing: that a coherent story about *why* a price/volume pattern should predict continuation ("committed buyers absorbing supply," "trapped longs forced to liquidate," "laggards catching up to breadth thrust") is enough to generate a real edge once you can articulate it and confirm it in-sample/walk-forward.
Evidence: EXP-001/002 (gap-and-go, momentum-continuation thesis), EXP-003/004 (PDH fade, mean-reversion thesis), EXP-005/006 (breadth-thrust, relative-strength thesis) — three *opposite* theses (continuation, fade, relative-strength) all cleared in-sample/walk-forward checks and then produced negative OOS expectancy (-312, -162, -208, -50, -43 per trade). The direction of the bet doesn't matter; something about the validation methodology itself is passing hypotheses that don't hold up.
Implication: Stop treating "good in-sample/walk-forward" as a signal worth reporting at all — it has now failed to predict OOS sign 6/6 times. The next round should either (a) require a genuinely held-out, chronologically later test as the *first* gate before any parameter tuning, or (b) treat in-sample fit as evidence of overfitting risk rather than edge, especially given how easy it is to construct a narrative that fits recent history.

**2. Layering filters onto a weak base signal reduces trade count, not loss-per-trade — it doesn't fix anything.**
Underlying assumption failing: that trend filters, fundamentals screens, and volume-confirmation thresholds "clean up" a mediocre base strategy by removing bad trades and keeping good ones.
Evidence: ORB-3 (daily trend filter: win rate 47.6%→47.7%, trades halved, loss halved proportionally), ORB-4 (fundamentals filter made recent-60-day result *worse*, -0.64%→-2.42%, because it removed some of the better performers), ORB-5 (volume confirmation made win rate *and* R:R worse as the threshold tightened, 45.1%→38.9%). In every case the filter acted like random thinning of the sample, not selection for quality.

## Additional Cross-Cutting Findings (beyond the established review)

**3. Mechanism designs with 3+ stacked conjunctive conditions are collapsing to statistically meaningless sample sizes before they ever get a fair OOS test.**
Underlying assumption failing: that adding more "confirming" conditions to a story (gap up AND above-average volume AND no VWAP retrace AND holds past 15 min; or PDH poke AND rel-vol spike AND two consecutive 5-min closes) makes the signal more precise without destroying its frequency.
Evidence: EXP-001 produced only 4 total trades (holdout below the 5-trade minimum); EXP-003 produced 0 trades in any window. In both cases the "reject" was really a "could not test" — the conjunction of rare conditions on a 29-symbol universe over the test window starved the sample before edge could even be evaluated. EXP-005/006 (breadth-thrust, also multi-condition) had enough trades to compute expectancy but still needed two rounds to get there.

## Additional Cross-Cutting Findings (beyond the established review, incorporating EXP-007/EXP-008)

**4. Both "continuation" and "reversion" stories built on the same underlying data (price/volume, same-instrument or index-breadth) fail OOS at similar rates — the direction of the bet is not the problem.**
Underlying assumption failing: that the lab just hasn't found the right *side* to play yet (momentum vs. fade). Look across the roster: EXP-001/002 (gap-and-go continuation, long bias) failed OOS; EXP-003/004 (failed-breakout fade, short bias) failed OOS; EXP-005/006 (relative-strength catch-up, bidirectional long/short) failed OOS; EXP-007/008 (VWAP-extension fade, bidirectional) failed OOS. That's every directional archetype available in a simple ORB-adjacent design space, all landing on negative OOS expectancy. This symmetry across opposite theses is itself informative: it's not that "breakouts fail so fades should work" or vice versa — both fail similarly, which points away from "wrong direction" as the diagnosis and toward "the signal-generation layer itself (intraday price/volume patterns on 5–15min bars for this universe) carries little real predictive content," at least in the way it's been operationalized so far.
Implication: Stop treating "try the opposite/mirror-image mechanism" as a fresh hypothesis. A mirrored fade of a rejected continuation idea (or vice versa) is not meaningfully novel and should not consume a full experiment slot unless there's a distinct causal story with a different data source, not just a sign-flip of the same VWAP/PDH/gap logic.

**5. "Wait for N confirming bars before entry" designs (a specific recurring sub-pattern of the already-flagged conjunction problem) fail for a distinct additional reason: lag, not just sample starvation.**
Underlying assumption failing: that requiring 2 consecutive 5-min closes/candles to "confirm" exhaustion or trend-holding improves signal quality for free. EXP-003 (two consecutive 5-min closes above PDH) → 0 trades; EXP-004, same mechanism → OOS expectancy -208.87; EXP-007 (two consecutive 5-min candles failing to print new extreme) → only 5 trades; EXP-008, same mechanism → 0/3 walk-forward windows positive. In every one of these four, the confirmation requirement was the specific ingredient (distinct from generic volume/fundamentals filters seen in the ORB seeds) that either starved the sample or arrived too late — by the time two bars confirm exhaustion/deceleration, the reversion/continuation move it's trying to catch has typically already happened, so the entries harvest the tail of the move rather than the move itself.
Implication: Treat "N-bar confirmation" as a red-flag mechanism component going forward, not a neutral quality filter. If a hypothesis needs multi-bar confirmation to define its entry, budget for the fact that this both shrinks the sample (per finding #3) *and* independently degrades expectancy through lag — two separate failure modes stacking, not one. Prefer single-bar, immediately-actionable triggers, or justify confirmation bars with an explicit lag-tolerance argument before running the full validation cycle.

**6. Threshold-sweeping on a single underlying signal family (ORB target multiple, volume multiple, ATR-extension multiple) has never once produced a config that is both statistically adequate and OOS-robust — it only ever trades overfitting-to-stale-data against sample collapse.**
Underlying assumption failing: that a fixed mechanism can be rescued by finding the "right" parameter value. SEED-ORB-2's sweep found a config that worked on 6 months but lost on the most recent 60 days. SEED-ORB-5's sweep found win rate and reward:risk *both* degrading as the threshold tightened, with trade counts falling to 18-29. EXP-007→EXP-008 tightened/held an ATR-extension multiple and went from 5 trades (can't validate) to 0/3 positive walk-forward windows (validated-and-failed). In three independent signal families now, sweeping a continuous threshold parameter has never surfaced a stable edge — it has only ever revealed the same over-fit/under-sampled dilemma in different clothing.
Implication: Deprioritize "sweep a threshold on an already-rejected or borderline mechanism" as a way to generate the next experiment. If round 1 of a mechanism is borderline, a parameter sweep alone should not count as sufficient additional evidence to greenlight it — the next hypothesis needs a structurally different signal (e.g., cross-sectional/relative-value ranking, order-flow/depth-based, options-derived positioning, overnight/gap information combined differently) rather than a retuned version of VWAP-distance, volume-multiple, or target-multiple on the same OHLCV bars. All 13 experiments so far have drawn their signal exclusively from same-instrument or index-breadth OHLCV data at 5–15 min resolution; that entire data-source class has yet to produce one durable OOS edge, which is reason enough to require the next batch to source signals from outside it.

EXP-009/EXP-010 (Intra-Sector Pair Spread Reversion, the first market-neutral pairs hypothesis, run through the new research_lab/pairs_simulator.py engine): REJECT on sample size (25 trades in 240 days, 1 OOS trade). Code-verified root cause: the hypothesis's own eligibility rule, trailing-60-day daily-return correlation > 0.8, is almost never satisfied by real NSE large-cap same-sector pairs -- HDFCBANK/ICICIBANK 0% of days, SUNPHARMA/CIPLA 0%, ULTRACEMCO/AMBUJACEM 9%, BAJFINANCE/SHRIRAMFIN 13%, TCS/INFY 49% (median correlations 0.4-0.6, only TCS/INFY ~0.8). Treat any future hypothesis whose gate assumes >0.8 daily-return correlation between two NSE stocks as sample-starved by construction. The z-score trigger itself was NOT the constraint.

EXP-011/EXP-012 (End-of-Day Reversal, Baltussen/Da/Soebhag 2025 -- the first hypothesis sourced from the academic literature rather than proposed by the Quant Researcher, and the first judged NET of transaction costs via research_lab/transaction_costs.py): REJECT. The effect itself replicates on NSE at roughly the published size -- 9,312 trades over 240 days, GROSS P&L +Rs.18,873 (~1 bp per position), in line with the paper's 2-3.5 bps per leg -- but Zerodha intraday charges plus a 2 bps/side spread cost Rs.257,403 (~14 bps per round trip), so the net result is -Rs.238,530 with 0/3 walk-forward windows positive. ESTABLISHED RULE (agreed 2026-09-07): an Indian cash intraday round trip costs ~10-14 bps regardless of position size (STT alone is 2.5 bps on the sell side), so any intraday hypothesis needs a documented GROSS edge of at least ~15 bps PER TRADE to be worth a full experiment. Every well-documented pure-intraday effect with data available to this lab (end-of-day reversal, market intraday momentum, interday half-hour momentum) sits in the 1-7 bps range and fails this bar by construction; the only candidates that clear it are event-driven (earnings-day moves) and those need announcement-TIME data the lab does not have. Intraday research is therefore paused in favour of swing research, where the same cost is negligible against multi-percent moves. Pool D continues as a framework test only.
